trigger: abilityLearned — a level-up rolls a new ability from the level pool
before: New trick: Viper —
after: New trick: Viper.
why: An event with no ability text left a dangling dash; the dash now appears only before real text.

trigger: abilityLearned — a level-up rolls a new ability from the level pool
before: New trick: Viper —
after: New trick: Viper.
why: The rail twin of the Oracle fix: no dangling dash when the event carries no text.

trigger: armorPatched — Sewing or a Master of Arms mends worn armour overnight
before: poisonedEdge: +2 back into your kit.
after: poisonedEdge: +2 armour patched back into your kit.
why: A bare "+2" never said what came back; it is armour, as the rail twin already said.

trigger: afflictionTick — a poison or disease takes its hp on a step
before: Poison (−2 hp).
after: Poison: still in you (−2 hp).
why: The rail printed "(−0 hp)" where its Oracle twin says the sickness has nothing left to take and you are on one hp; the two now say the same thing, and a tick says what did it.

trigger: campFailed — Make Camp is refused for want of rations
before: You eat 5 a night (Your companion eats 1 more). You have 10. Find rations first.
after: Not enough food to make camp: the party eats 5 a night (Your companion eats 1 of those), and you have 10. Find rations first.
why: The refusal never named the camp it refused, and the engine's need is the whole party's night, so "you eat N (Mira eats 1 more)" counted the member twice.

trigger: campFailed — Make Camp is refused for want of rations
before: You eat 5 a night, you have 10. Find rations first.
after: Not enough food to make camp: you eat 5 a night, you have 10. Find rations first.
why: The rail twin now names the refused camp, and a party's night reads "the party eats".

trigger: chestLocked — the lock roll on a chest fails
before: Not today. The lock wins this round.
after: The lock holds, and the box stays shut for good. Not today, and not any other day.
why: A chest gets one lock roll and its tile is cleared first, so "this round" promised a retry that never comes; the fact now comes before the joke.

trigger: chestLocked — the lock roll on a chest fails
before: The lock wins this round.
after: The lock holds. The box stays shut for good.
why: The rail twin of the Oracle fix: a failed lock is final.

trigger: darknessFell — a Darkness result on the dot falls on the hero
before: The dark closes in around you.
after: The dark closes in around you: you see only the squares beside you, and you fight worse in it.
why: The line never said what the dark does or how long it lasts; it now states the cost, the event's duration in squares, and that Night Vision waives it.

trigger: equipRejected — the Gear tab refuses to equip an item
before: Not for the likes of you. Dagger refuses your hands — your kind wears no armour.
after: Your kind wears no armour, so Dagger stays off. Not for the likes of you.
why: Every reason now says why in the player's terms before the joke: the class armour rule (tooHeavy) and the class weapon rule no longer read as a bare "Not for the likes of you", an unequippable item says so, and the Woodsman's rule is named.

trigger: equipRejected — the Gear tab refuses to equip an item
before: Too heavy to carry.
after: Your class does not wear that armour.
why: tooHeavy is the class armour rule (engine/items.js#armorRefusalReason), not weight; wrongClass now says it is your class, and a Woodsman's rule names plate as well as mail.

trigger: foeStoned — an Amulet of Stone or Oak Staff turns foes to stone
before: It turn to stone. Statues don't hit back.
after: It turns to stone. Statues don't hit back.
why: One stoned foe read "Grunk turn to stone"; the verb now agrees with the count.

trigger: foeStoned — an Amulet of Stone or Oak Staff turns foes to stone
before: It turn to stone. Statues don't hit back.
after: It turns to stone. Statues don't hit back.
why: The rail twin of the Oracle fix: one foe "turns".

trigger: insanityRage — the hero's insanity rolls a rage
before: Rage: +2 might.
after: Rage: +2 damage on every blow until the day ends.
why: "Might" is engine vocabulary; the line now says it is damage on every blow and lasts until the new day clears it.

trigger: insanityRage — the hero's insanity rolls a rage
before: Rage: +2 might.
after: Rage: +2 damage on every blow until the day ends.
why: The rail twin of the Oracle fix.

trigger: insanityRolled — an Insanity result on the dot rolls the hero's d6
before: Insanity. It comes apart at the seams.
after: Insanity takes hold of you.
why: The line printed the INSANITY table's foe-side row ("It strikes the nearest of its own") for the hero's own insanity; it now says it is yours, and faces 2, 4 and 6, which do nothing, say so.

trigger: insanityRolled — an Insanity result on the dot rolls the hero's d6
before: Insanity — it comes apart.
after: Insanity takes hold of you.
why: The rail twin of the Oracle fix.

trigger: itemEffectStarted — a worn or drunk item's timed effect starts
before: Unseen for 3 squares. They need two better.
after: Unseen for 3 squares: every foe has two fewer faces that hit you.
why: The Anklet's "need two better" was roll-under and the Cloak's line never said what being unseen does; both now use their item text's roll-high words, a count of one reads "1 square", and a bare event no longer leaks "undefined squares".

trigger: itemEffectStarted — a worn or drunk item's timed effect starts
before: Unseen for 3 squares. They need two better.
after: Unseen for 3 squares: every foe has two fewer faces that hit you.
why: The rail twin of the Oracle fix, the Cloak of Invisibility's effect in the rail's short form.

trigger: itemRejected — a take or a store buy is refused
before: Not an upgrade. Dagger.
after: Not an upgrade: Dagger is no better than what you have.
why: The same refusal reader as equipRejected: the stilted "Not an upgrade. Dagger." reads naturally, and the class rules say why before the joke.

trigger: itemRejected — a take or a store buy is refused
before: Too heavy to carry.
after: Your class does not wear that armour.
why: The same fix as rail:equipRejected: tooHeavy is the class armour rule, not weight (79-09 handoff).

trigger: joinerMet — a Joiner is met on the dot
before: Viper, a Apprentice, joins you for a while.
after: Viper, an Apprentice, offers to travel with you for a while.
why: The meeting is an offer that the accept, decline or refusal follows, so "joins you" contradicted a decline; the article agrees, and a real event states the Joiner's level.

trigger: joinerRefused — a Magic User Joiner will not travel with a Wilmsry
before: Viper takes one look at a Wilmsry and leaves.
after: Viper, a Magic User, takes one look at a Wilmsry and leaves.
why: The refusal never said why; it now names the Magic User, as the Oracle twin does.

trigger: the rail card after the first Android back press on a live run
before: Press back once more and this delve is abandoned. Nobody will write it down.
after: Press back once more to close the game. The delve waits for you.
why: A second back press closes the app and the run is already saved, so nothing is abandoned; it now matches the Oracle line 79-10 fixed (79-10 handoff).

trigger: rationsBought — rations bought at the store
before: Stocked up: +1 rations.
after: Stocked up: +1 ration.
why: "+1 rations" is now "+1 ration", as on the Oracle.

trigger: staffRecharged — a staff regains a charge
before: Crystal Staff hums. 2/5.
after: Crystal Staff hums: a charge is back (2/5).
why: A bare "2/5" never said what it counted, and a bare event printed "?/?".

trigger: staffRecharged — a staff regains a charge
before: Crystal Staff hums. 2/5.
after: Crystal Staff hums: a charge is back (2/5).
why: The rail twin of the Oracle fix.

trigger: storeOpened — the store opens
before: The shop is open. (A discount, as always.)
after: The shop is open. (Half price, as always.)
why: The discount never said how much (half), and a Pickpocket's ×1.25 buy and ×0.75 sell prices were on the rail but missing from the Oracle.

trigger: storeOpened — the store opens
before: Shop open. (a discount, as always)
after: Shop open. (half price, as always)
why: The rail twin of the Oracle fix: the discount says how much.

trigger: trapDisarmed — a Pilfer disarms a trap
before: A Pilfer's hands already knew where not to put themselves.
after: Pilfer: trap disarmed. Your hands already knew where not to put themselves.
why: The joke stood in for the fact; the line now says the trap was disarmed first.

trigger: trapDoubled — a Cat Burglar's trap hits twice as hard
before: Cat Burglar's luck holds — for the trap. It hits twice as hard.
after: Cat Burglar: the trap hits twice as hard. The luck holds — for the trap.
why: The fact now comes before the joke.

trigger: trapPoisoned — a trap's arrow poisons the hero
before: Trap: it leaves something behind that outlasts the bruise.
after: Trap: poisoned. It leaves something behind that outlasts the bruise.
why: The line never said "poisoned"; the fact now comes before the joke.

trigger: useRefused — an item's use is refused
before: Dagger: 3 squares. It is not a vending machine.
after: Dagger: ready again in 3 squares. It is not a vending machine.
why: A bare "3 squares" never said it was the wait until the item is ready; an explore-only item now says it only works out of a fight.

trigger: useRefused — an item's use is refused
before: Dagger needs quieter surroundings.
after: Dagger only works out of a fight. It needs quieter surroundings.
why: The rail twin of the Oracle fix: the rule before the joke, and the cooldown reads "ready again in".

trigger: wentHungry — the new day finds too few rations
before: Hunger: nobody packed — you eat 5 a night, and you had 10. Cost of living −4 hp.
after: Hunger: you eat 5 a night, and you had 10. Nobody packed enough. Cost of living −4 hp.
why: The joke came before the numbers and read false when you had some rations; the numbers now come first.

trigger: wentHungry — the new day finds too few rations
before: Hunger: no rations (−4 hp).
after: Hunger: not enough rations (−4 hp).
why: Hunger fires when you have fewer rations than the night needs, not only none.
